chunks.arabic_text: ٢٩ - مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ، الْجَامُورَانِيُّ، أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، الرَّازِي. ضَعَّفَهُ الْقُمِّيُونَ، وَاسْتَثْنَوْا مِنْ كِتَابِ "نَوَادِرِ الْحِكْمَةِ" مَا رَوَاهُ. وَفِي مَذْهَبِهِ ارْتِفَاعٌ.

translations.en: 29 – Muḥammad b. Aḥmad, al-Jāmūrānī, Abū ʿAbdillāh, al-Rāzī. The Qummis weakened him, and they excluded what he narrated from the book “Nawādir al-Ḥikma”. In his madhhab there is irtifāʿ.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* highlights Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-Jāmūrānī, a prominent figure from Rayy whose reliability was contested by the Qum school of hadith scholars. While the Qumites deemed him weak (ḍaʿīf) and excluded his narrations from *Nawādir al-Ḥikma*, the mention of 'irtifāʿ' (elevation) suggests a nuanced scholarly debate regarding his status, possibly indicating high rank in specific contexts despite the criticism. This reflects the broader Shia tradition of evaluating narrators based on regional scholarly consensus and specific theological or jurisprudential alignments.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Jamurani and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الْقُمِّيُونَ: The scholars of Qum, a major center of Shia scholarship
key_terms.نَوَادِرُ الْحِكْمَةِ: Nawadir al-Hikma, a specific book of hadith
key_terms.مَذْهَبِهِ: His school of thought or scholarly status
key_terms.ارْتِفَاعٌ: Elevation or high status (technical term in ʿilm al-rijāl)
